title: Fallback routing and burst mitigation after reserved pool depletion
creator: Asha Venkataraman
description:
Summary: Multiple customer escalations during a March traffic spike revealed that Dedicated reserved GPU pools were not correctly triggering fallback routing or burst capacity policies. Customers experienced elevated 5xx rates and throttling for short windows (1–5m) when a pool transitioned from healthy to depleted. This ticket tracks the bug triage, an immediate mitigation plan, and the production fix rollout.

Context: The Dedicated allocator marks a pool as depleted when its available reservation tokens reach zero. During high-concurrency bursts, we observed a race where outgoing requests still held tokens but the pool was reported depleted due to async accounting (expiry window + GC). The router policy then avoided routing to that pool and did not engage the configured burst fallback path (reserved burst queue and cross-pool spillover). As a result, requests were rejected instead of being redirected to burst capacity or compatible model variants.

Observed impact:
- Two enterprise customers (support tickets #INC-2148, #INC-2151) saw a 25–40% increase in request failures during two separate peak periods (2026-03-09 17:24 UTC and 2026-03-10 13:02 UTC).
- Error signature: downstream errors with code 503 + router msg: "no-suitable-pool" and allocator logs: "pool_depleted: true (tokens: 0, pending: 27)".
- Latency spikes for successfully routed requests were 3–4x normal due to frantic fallback attempts.

This ticket will:
1) ship a hotfix to restore correct routing behavior for short depletion windows,
2) deploy an admission-control throttle to reduce cascading failures while fallback engages, and
3) add deterministic tests and observability to prevent regressions.
root_cause_summary: A race between token expiry GC and pool accounting caused 'pool_depleted' to be set while in-flight requests still held tokens. The router checks pool availability atomically against stale metadata and chooses to avoid the pool, but the fallback routing code path expects the allocator to advertise 'burst_available'. A missing atomic decrement/compare-and-swap on the reservation token counter plus a logic gap in router fallback selection produced an effective blackhole for requests during short depletion windows.
mitigation_actions: Hotfix v1 (2026-03-11): change allocator GC window from 2s to 200ms and make pool_depleted transition hysteresis 500ms to avoid flapping during high burst concurrency.
Immediate config change: enable cross-pool spillover for affected enterprise customers to allow requests to be routed to other Dedicated pools in the same region.
Oncall rollback plan: toggle 'strict_pool_isolation' to false for short windows via feature flag in console to allow graceful routing to compatible pools.
Run incident-specific canary that replays customer traffic in staging to validate fixes before prod rollout.
long_term_fixes: Implement atomic reservation token updates with CAS in allocator and add unit tests for concurrent acquire/release scenarios.
Revise router selection to consult a consistent pool health snapshot that includes 'burst_available' and 'pending_releases' before making decisions.
Add admission-control queue at edge that enforces a short-term throttling policy when pool depletion is detected, preventing cascade failures across services.
Add e2e test harness for reserved-pool exhaustion that runs in CI and nightly chaos tests to assert fallback behavior under load.
Telemetry: emit 'pool_transition' events with versioned schema (v2) and surface in Console as per-route SLO breach alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix v2 deployed to prod with allocator CAS and router snapshot fix in runtime-1.21 can be reverted without incidents.
No customer-facing 5xx spikes (>=15min window) related to pool depletion during two 72h post-rollout simulated high-burst tests.
New telemetry exposes 'pool_flap_rate', 'burst_spill_rate', and 'admission_throttle_count' in Console dashboards.
PR reviews completed and security review (if requested) signed off.

Observed that 'reserved_burst_limit' config was set conservatively for some customers; product to review SLA expectations.
We agreed to keep strict_pool_isolation=false for affected customers until final fix (feature flag: ff.strict_pool_isolation).
